nodes.label: Proposed simulation improvements and research priorities
nodes.rationale: Proposes execution-contract verification and causal diagnostics before broader entry/exit experiments. Its $1,000 capital and $100 drawdown requirements describe the historical baseline, and no new implementation or backtests are claimed.

nodes.label: Versioned broker price and entry-execution contract
nodes.rationale: Twenty-seven impossible entry intervals motivate verifying instrument, order-type and date-specific order precision; locally triggered IOC versus broker-native behavior; and separation of price limits, displacement and fees. A justified model correction requires consistent rules and rejection audits, not improved P&L or forced fills.

nodes.label: Causal order diagnostics and execution-state timing
nodes.rationale: Proposes separate event, receipt, decision, submission, activation, fill-report and cancellation-acknowledgment times. Strategy knowledge can differ from actual simulated holdings. Quote marks must be distinguished from capacity-constrained liquidation; isolated delay sensitivities, partial-fill replenishment and fill/cancel races need explicit treatment.

nodes.label: Registered evidence expansion and controlled hypotheses
nodes.rationale: Requires prespecified historical membership, coverage and corporate-action checks, retained exclusions, independent symbol-dates, prospective clock evidence and dependency-aware precision criteria. Entry extension, exit geometry, revalidation and selection are bounded strategy hypotheses to attribute individually before testing a combination on untouched evidence.

nodes.label: Alpaca order documentation
nodes.rationale: The report cites two-decimal limit-price precision at or above $1 and four decimals below $1 as broker-specific order-entry documentation, explicitly not a universal data tick rule or confirmation of the intended broker.
